newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Six killed on Tajik-Afghan border, ceasefire shaky.
newsitem.headline: Six killed on Tajik-Afghan border, ceasefire shaky.

text.p: Russian-led guards patrolling the border between Tajikistan and Afghanistan killed six people who tried to cross the frontier, the border guards' press service said on Monday.
It said five people had been killed on Sunday as they tried to cross the Pyandzh River which separates the two countries. Two assault rifles, some detonators and explosives were found on the dead.
A sixth person was killed in a separate incident further along the border.

It was not clear if the six belonged to Tajikistan's armed Islamic opposition, who have fought the Russian-backed government in a bloody four-year civil war. The border is also widely used by drug smugglers.
The latest upsurge of fighting in Afghanistan has heightened tensions along the remote border in the Pamir mountains, guarded by thousands of Russian-led troops.

Tajik military sources said presidential guards manning a post in the village of Obi-Garm, 80 km (50 miles) east of the Tajik capital Dushanbe, came under attack early on Monday. One guard was killed and two were wounded.

The sources said around 30 opposition guerrillas carried out the attack but said it was not sanctioned by the opposition leadership, who are currently adhering to a shaky United Nations-sponsored ceasefire reconfirmed in July.
There was no immediate comment from the Tajik opposition.
